note: [agent-bulk] numucc_em. Only ONE shower in scope: 17012 (pdg 11, kine_charge 396.8 MeV, 12 seg, cluster 17+48+49) -- the other 11 showers are all sub-20 MeV 2-point stubs and I did not look at them. Vertex is good: judged from the vtx-* sweep at 92.7 cm half-span (r95 74.2, no vtxz frames -- event under the 150 cm trigger). The blue star sits exactly where the 79.1 cm pdg-13 track 17013 ends and the EM cone begins; the shower start X coincides with it, and az-055 and az+085 both show a single apex there. 17013 (the muon) is grey/unowned -- correctly NOT swallowed, so no over-clustering of a MIP stem. Members cover the whole visible cone and the yellow set has one apex and one direction in both azimuths. Under-clustering checked on the non-members: every unowned segment other than 17013 is either a 0.1-0.5 cm delta stub lying along the muon at 109-172 deg from the axis (44022 12.5 cm/109.3, 45023, 42020, 53040, 47025, 43021, 50039, 46024 out to 82 cm), or 17014, a 5.3 cm pdg-211 stub leaving the vertex at ~85 deg to the shower axis. Nothing grey sits in the forward cone. Membership triple-checked: nseg 12 == the 12 segments with owner 17012 == the 12 candidate rows carrying owner 17012. Two pdg-2212 rows are inside the member set (49038, 3.6 cm, in the shower's own cluster 49; 48026, a 0.1 cm 2-point stub at 22.8 cm / 18.8 deg) -- both tiny and forward, I do not read them as over-clustering. No pi0: no second EM object anywhere in the event, so no pio judgement is offered. Verdict is about clustering only and silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] numucc_em, 33 showers. Verdict shower 17067 (pdg 11, kine_charge 252.1, 10 seg) -- the first pdg-11 entry of in_scope. I PASSED OVER the higher-charge in-scope object 17023 (pdg 13, kine_charge 455.2, kine_best 635.7, 276 cm over 2 segments): it is the muon, drawn blue, running from the vertex to the far wall, and it is not an EM shower. The other 31 showers are all sub-20 MeV and I did not look at them. Vertex judged off the vtxz-* frames (60 cm half-span, auto-fired: r95 251.9 cm, so the vtx-* set at 314.8 cm half-span is useless here). It is good: three prongs converge on the star -- the muon 17023, the 30 cm pdg-13 track 17028, and 17067's stem -- and the shower start X sits on it. CLUSTERING: nothing is missing and nothing foreign is swallowed. Membership triple-checked and all three agree: nseg 10 == owner-grouped 10 == cmp_div 10 segments plotted (0.0-34.2 cm, 0.0-45.7 deg). Every non-member near the shower is off-axis: 61060 85.5deg, 55054 141.2, 45044 49.4, 53052 78.5, 60059 71.9, then 54053/56055/57056/58057/52051 at 75-90 deg, 48047 29.3, 47046 49.5, 63063 38.9. The one on-axis-looking grey object, 17028 (pdg 13, unowned, candidate row d=8.1 cm / ang 2.5 deg, site 'in_main_cluster (walk_excl...)'), is NOT under-clustering: that row reports where the segment STARTS, and the segment itself is a 30.1 cm straight track leaving the stem at the 8 cm branch point and running perpendicular to the shower axis (-43.1,-36.9,252.2) -> (-43.8,-65.7,252.1), i.e. pure -y. It is the third vertex prong and is correctly left grey. START/AXIS WRONG is the finding worth the owner's eye here, and it is about the axis, not the clustering: the reco axis is dir15, fixed by the first 15 cm of the chain, and the object then bends ~37 deg over its next 18 cm, so its own far members 17019/17031 land at 33.4 cm / 45.7 deg -- visible on the acceptance plot as an accepted orange square sitting far above the 25 deg pass-1 step, admitted only by cluster connectivity (in_main_cluster walk_add), not by any cone. The alternative reading I could not fully exclude, and the one I would let the owner reverse: that 17067 fuses a diffuse ~15 cm vertex blob with a separate straight 23 cm piece (17018, straightness 0.98) plus its terminal blob, i.e. over-clustered. I rejected it because all three viewpoints (az-055/el+20, az+085/el+20, az-055/el+65) show continuous point cloud through the bend with no gap, the bend is gradual (40 deg then 34 deg across two short segments, not one elbow), and a 16 deg off-axis satellite 62062 is absorbed at 34 cm, which is shower-like rather than track-like. No pi0: the event has no reco pi0 group and no second EM object; the kine_pio_* block names E1 0.1 MeV, which is noise, and is not a pairing -- I offer no pi0 judgement. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] nuecc, 24 showers, 2 in scope. Verdict shower 18092 (pdg 11, kine_charge 604.0, 34 seg) -- the first pdg-11 entry of in_scope and also the highest-charge object. The other in-scope object 18009 (pdg 13, kine_charge 74.2, 64.8 cm) is discussed below; the 22 skipped showers are all sub-20 MeV and I did not look at them. Vertex judged off the vtx-* sweep at 137.9 cm half-span (r95 110.3, under the 150 cm trigger so no vtxz-* frames were written). OVER-CLUSTERED: 18092's member set contains a backward branch that its own cone does not reach. Taking the shower's own axis as vertex -> centroid of the other 32 members, direction (-0.043,-0.426,0.904), those 32 members lie at 0.3-47.3 deg from it (only the seed 18092 at the vertex reaches 47, everything else is under 16 deg) and run out to 137 cm -- a tight, coherent cone. Against that same axis 18015 sits at 129-179 deg and 18008 at 176-179 deg, i.e. directly BEHIND the shower start. They are also detached from the shower's own body: nearest member point 10.9 cm away for 18015 and 14.7 cm for 18008, while both touch the 64.8 cm pdg-13 track 18009 (gap 0.25 cm and 0.00 cm -- 18008's endpoint IS 18009's endpoint at (120.0,142.4,348.2)). Neither entered through the cone: the acceptance plot shows them at 13 cm/33.5 deg and 15 cm/58 deg, both above the 30 deg pass-1 box, absorbed by pass3_cluster_map (direct) and conn3_unreachable (walk_add). MARKS, and they differ in strength (correction 7): 18015 OUT is the strong one -- 17.3 cm, 30 fitted points, owned only by 18092, and the one that carries the charge. 18008 OUT is the weak one and the one I would let the owner reverse: it is 5.4 cm and it is ALSO one of 18009's two members (18009 nseg 2, owner-grouped 1, cmp_div 2), so it is a shared segment in correction-11's sense, not something 18092 took from a neighbour. NOT under-clustered: every unowned segment near the shower is a 0.1-1.2 cm two-point stub, the closest sitting 5.4 cm off the member set, and the nearest substantial ones are 8.5-9.4 cm out. Membership triple-checked for 18092: nseg 34 == owner-grouped 34 == cmp_div 34 (0.0-137.0 cm, 0.0-126.3 deg -- that 126 deg is measured against the RECO axis, which is wrong; see next). START/AXIS WRONG on 18092 as well: the reco axis points roughly opposite to the shower's own body, which is why almost every genuine member is tabulated at 106-126 deg and was let in by pass3_cone rather than by any pass-1 step. THE SECOND FINDING I COULD NOT SETTLE, and the reason this is 'likely' not 'certain': 18009 is a 64.8 cm pdg-13 skeleton running at only 10 deg to the shower body, passing within 1.8 cm of the vertex and lying INSIDE the same dense charge blob as 18092's own skeleton -- two parallel skeletons in one blob. Either it is a genuine second particle, or it is the electron's own MIP stem split off from its shower, in which case 18092 is also under-clustered and the verdict would be 'both'. I could not separate those two readings from the three viewpoints I looked at, so I recorded only the finding I could measure. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] nuecc, small event (r95 28.4 cm, 8 segments, 6 showers). Only ONE shower in scope: 21011 (pdg 11, kine_charge 101.4, 3 seg) -- the 5 skipped showers are all sub-20 MeV and every one of them is a 0.2-0.8 cm two-point stub, which I confirmed from the segment table rather than looking at them individually. Vertex judged off the vtx-* sweep at 35.5 cm half-span (no vtxz-* frames: the event is far under the 150 cm trigger). It is good -- the star sits at the single apex where the shower's only stem begins and there is no other prong anywhere in the event. CORRECT: the member set is one contiguous chain from the vertex, seed 21011 running 22.9 cm out to dvtx 20.6, then an 8.1 cm branch 21003 and a 1.1 cm stub 53005 attached at its far end (both tier 1, 16.5/19.1 cm at 17.2/18.4 deg, in_main_cluster walk_add and pass3_cone). Membership triple-checked: nseg 3 == owner-grouped 3 == cmp_div 3 (0.0-19.1 cm, 0.0-18.4 deg). Nothing is missing: the four non-members anywhere near it are 57009 (0.6 cm, gap 4.6 cm, 34.1 deg), 56008 (0.8 cm pdg 2212, gap 10.4 cm, 128.9 deg), 55007 (0.2 cm, gap 16.6 cm, 55.5 deg) and 54006 (0.6 cm, gap 34.7 cm, 28.4 deg) -- all two-point stubs, all off-axis, none contiguous. The one shape feature worth naming: 21003 doubles back at 131 deg to the seed's own direction, so in projection the object reads as a lambda with its apex at the FAR end rather than at the vertex. I checked it from az-055/el+20 and az+085/el+20 and it is a short branch hanging off the far end of one stem, not a symmetric V of two prongs meeting away from the vertex, so I did not read it as a second apex. No pi0: no reco group and no second EM object in the event. 4 frames looked at, which is the right cost for a three-segment single-shower event. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID -- I note only that 101 MeV in a thin ~20 cm object is not obviously shower-like, and I did NOT compute a density from kine_charge/length.

[agent-bulk] other_em, 15 showers, 2 in scope. Verdict shower 18011 (pdg 11, kine_charge 170.0, 7 seg) -- the first pdg-11 entry of in_scope. I PASSED OVER the other in-scope object 26015 (pdg 2212, kine_charge 107.7, 11.4 cm), which is not an EM shower and in any case sits 337 cm away in a completely separate blob at (201,57,140) -- it plays no part in this judgement. The 13 skipped showers are sub-20 MeV. Vertex judged off the vtxz-* frames (60 cm half-span, auto-fired: r95 340.2 cm, and note event_half_span_cm reads 400.0 because it saturates -- correction 19). Clean single-photon topology: the star sits ~18 cm from the shower with essentially nothing at it -- only 57036 (0.8 cm pdg 2212 exactly on the vertex), 46017 (0.2 cm at 4.1 cm) and 48019 (0.7 cm at 4.6 cm), a very low-energy recoil. There is no prong to check convergence against, so I do not call the vertex bad; I only note there is almost no charge there. CORRECT. The member set is a compact conversion blob -- six contiguous cluster-18 segments (all mutual gaps 0.00 cm) inside a 9.3 cm radius of their centroid (-87.7,-77.9,19.8) -- plus 59032, a 5.7 cm 11-point fragment 24.4 cm further out, absorbed by pass4_angle at 39.5 cm / 24.9 deg, which the acceptance plot puts just UNDER the 25 deg step. Membership triple-checked: nseg 7 == owner-grouped 7 == cmp_div 7 (0.0-39.5 cm, 0.0-37.2 deg). The alternative reading I considered and rejected: that 59032 is a separate object and 18011 is over-clustered. I rejected it because 59032 lies on the photon's line of flight -- the direction nu-vertex -> blob centroid and the direction blob centroid -> 59032 agree to 12.3 deg -- so it is where a late shower fragment belongs, not a coincidence. Not under-clustered: every unowned segment near the shower is a 0.2-1.8 cm two-point/four-point stub. The one item a stricter scanner could mark IN, and I deliberately did not: 45016, a 0.3 cm two-point stub 7.9 cm past 59032 at 50.0 cm / 25.9 deg -- the acceptance plot shows it as a circle sitting just OUTSIDE the 25 deg step, which is exactly the corroboration pattern the brief names, but at two points and 0.3 cm it carries no charge worth the mark and marking it would flip the event's bucket on nothing. No pi0: no reco group, and the only other EM object in the event is 337 cm away. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] nuecc, and the whole event is THREE segments, so this judgement is complete rather than a fast pass. Verdict shower 11000 (pdg 11, kine_charge 107.5, ONE segment, 35.8 cm, 61 fitted points) -- the only pdg-11 entry of in_scope. The two skipped showers are the only other segments in the event and I accounted for both: 35002, a zero-length two-point pdg-2212 stub 16.9 cm from the vertex at 136.7 deg (behind the shower), and 15001, a 0.4 cm stub 446.9 cm away at 170.7 deg. Vertex judged off the vtx-* sweep at 40.1 cm half-span (r95 32.0, far under the 150 cm trigger, so no vtxz-*). The star sits at the base of the one object in the event; there is no second prong, so nothing can contradict it. CORRECT, and trivially checkable: nseg 1 == owner-grouped 1 == cmp_div 1, so nothing foreign can have been swallowed, and there is no contiguous unclaimed charge anywhere -- the nearest non-member is 16.9 cm away, behind the start, and carries no length. 3 frames looked at, which is the right cost here (correction 13); the shower frames cover the whole event at this scale. What I am NOT saying: the object is a single narrow straight ribbon of charge with uniform width, no cone, no branching and no terminal blob, which does not LOOK like a shower. That is a PID question the display cannot settle for me, so this verdict is about clustering and carries no PID claim -- I did not compute a density from kine_charge/length (correction 18), and I note only that a ~107 MeV electron is barely above the LAr critical energy and legitimately stays narrow over its first couple of radiation lengths, so 'thin' is not evidence against pdg 11 here. No pi0: one EM object in the event, no reco group.

[agent-bulk] numucc_em, 28 showers, 5 in scope (14007, 28036, 60050, 64054, 50049 -- all pdg 11). Verdict shower 14007 (kine_charge 616.1, 5 seg) -- the first pdg-11 entry of in_scope and the highest-charge object in the event; no non-EM object outranks it. The 23 skipped showers are sub-20 MeV, but many of them ARE the subject of this finding, so I read them off the segment table rather than treating them as unlooked-at. Vertex judged off the vtx-* sweep at 126.8 cm half-span (r95 101.4, under the 150 cm trigger, no vtxz-*). It is good: the star sits at the apex of a clean two-armed V -- the 88.8 cm pdg-13 track 14001 (unowned, correctly grey) on one arm and the shower on the other, and the shower start X sits 3.7 cm from it. UNDER-CLUSTERED. 14007's own skeleton stops at 41.6 cm from the vertex (members 14007, 14073, 14010, 14011, 14008; cmp_div 0.0-33.9 cm from the start, 0.0-11.5 deg). Beyond that, along the shower's OWN axis (vertex -> member centroid = (-0.034,0.723,0.690)), there is a train of about 25 segments at 7-25 deg running out to 102 cm, split among ~15 separate objects: 60050 (50.9 MeV), 28036 (58.4), 64054 (38.2), 50049 (35.5) and a dozen singleton sub-20 MeV showers (49048, 63053, 78068, 46045, 48047, 47046, 76066, 77067, 80070, 72062, 79069, 68058). For a 616 MeV EM shower that pattern reads as a shredded tail, not as fifteen particles. The corroboration the brief asks for is on the acceptance plot: 49048 is a CIRCLE at 25.8 cm / 7.4 deg, well inside the 15 deg pass-1 gate, and 50049 is a circle at 41.7 cm / 15.0 deg sitting exactly ON it -- two non-members inside or on the gate. MARKS, IN, and they differ in strength (correction 7): 50049 IN is the strong one -- 3.5 cm, 7 fitted points, the seed of its own 35.5 MeV shower, 5.5 cm from 14007's skeleton and on the gate line. 49048 IN is the weak one and the one I would let the owner reverse -- it sits deepest inside the cone (6.5 deg to the own-axis, 4.5 cm gap) but it is a 0.2 cm two-point stub carrying no charge, so it changes the energy by nothing. NOT MARKED but named: 60050 (4.4 cm / 9 points, 50.9 MeV, gap 6.1 cm) is as close as those two but sits at 24.4 deg to the own axis, outside the 15 deg gate, so a mark on it would over-claim; and 28036 (7.9 cm / 14 points, 58.4 MeV, 10.2 deg) is on-axis but 13.6 cm off the skeleton. Correction 11/16 caveat, stated because it is the main risk here: none of this charge is grey -- every piece is owned by a neighbouring shower or is the seed of its own sub-20 MeV shower, which is exactly the unsafe basis the corrections warn about. I ran the triple-check on 14007 and all three agree (nseg 5 == owner-grouped 5 == cmp_div 5), so the display is not lying about ownership and these really are non-members; my claim is the physics one, that the reconstruction should have merged them, not that the table is wrong. PI0: the reco has NO pi0 group (every pio_id is -1), so the [14007, 28036] pair in the pio-* frames is the capture's automatic top-two slotting (correction 3) and not the reconstruction's pairing. Priced, it fails: the display gives m = 62.9 MeV on the axis convention (theta 19.1 deg) and 29.5 MeV on the vertex convention (theta 8.9 deg), and for E1 616.1 / E2 58.4 the opening angle needed for 135 MeV is 41.7 deg. So 28036 cannot be the partner gamma of 14007, which removes the innocent explanation for a second EM object sitting 10 deg off the leading shower's axis and supports the under-clustering reading. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] nuecc, small event (r95 25.6 cm, 8 segments, 6 showers). Only ONE shower in scope: 3002 (pdg 11, kine_charge 166.2, 3 seg, 29.1 cm). Of the 5 skipped showers, four are 0.2-0.3 cm two-point stubs (29004 pdg 2212 at 12.5 cm/70.8 deg, 32007 at 19.5/25.7, 28003 at 24.1/105.1, 31006 at 52.9/96.2) and the fifth, 3008, is the substance of this entry. 3 frames looked at (az-055/el+20, az+085/el+20, az-055/el+65); the event is 26 cm across so the shower frames contain all of it including the vertex marker, and I did not open the vtx-* sweep separately -- the budget is a ceiling (correction 13). Vertex is good: 3002 and 3008 BOTH begin exactly on the star at (-82.2,22.2,79.5), so the star is the apex of the only two prongs in the event. CORRECT. The member set is a clean single cone: 3002 (13.5 cm) from the vertex out to 12.8 cm, then 3001 (15.1 cm, 1.6 deg to the axis) out to 25.6 cm, with the point cloud narrow at the start and broadening along it in all three views. Membership triple-checked: nseg 3 == owner-grouped 3 == cmp_div 3 (0.0-34.6 cm, 0.0-24.6 deg). THE ONE ITEM WORTH THE OWNER'S EYE, and the one I would let them reverse: 3008 -- 5.6 cm, 10 fitted points, kine_charge 29.9 MeV (18% of the shower's), reco pdg 11, in the SAME cluster 3 as the shower, touching the shower start at gap 0.00 cm, and left out as its own sub-20 MeV shower (kine_best 14.2, which is why the scope rule skipped it). This is exactly correction 16's case, so I settled it the prescribed way: the triple-check above says it is genuinely a non-member, not an ownership artefact. Two readings, and I chose between them rather than hiding behind unclear. (a) it is the second prong of the neutrino vertex -- correctly excluded; (b) it is the electron's own near-vertex charge broken off -- under-clustered by 30 MeV. I took (a): 3008 leaves the vertex at 30 deg to the shower's first leg, and 30 deg is not electron behaviour 0-5 cm from a shower start, where the electron is still a single narrow MIP stem (the picture confirms the stem is narrow there); a 30 MeV prong at that angle at the vertex reads as a second particle. It does lie inside the shower's near-vertex cloud in the el+65 projection, which is why I call this 'likely' and not 'certain'. ALSO NOT MARKED: 30005, a 0.5 cm two-point pdg-13 stub absorbed by pass3_cone at 34.6 cm / 24.6 deg, i.e. 9 cm past where the shower's own members stop -- a marginal over-absorption carrying negligible charge, named here rather than marked. No pi0: one EM cone in the event and no reco group. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.
